speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your sudden vertigo, can you describe exactly what the sensation feels like—for example, does the room seem to spin around you, or do you feel like you are swaying or lightheaded? Also, did this episode start suddenly while you were moving your head or changing position?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To help narrow down the cause, did you experience any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in one ear during or after the episode? Additionally, do you have any history of migraines or recent head trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the episode lasted about 3 minutes and started while you were going to bed; did the spinning sensation specifically trigger when you turned your head or rolled over in bed? Also, have you noticed any weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking since the episode ended?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver on the left side, combined with the brief duration of symptoms and lack of other neurological signs, strongly points to a mechanical issue in the inner ear. Based on these findings, I am confident in my assessment.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
